summary: Rahul Sankrityayan (1893–1963) worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He taught Sanskrit at Vidyalankara Pirivena (1927) and held posts at Saint Petersburg State University (1937, 1945–1947) and its Faculty of Oriental Studies (circa 1937–1947).

Raimo Anttila (1935–2023) was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied at Yale University under Warren Crawford Cowgill (circa 1962–1966) and held positions at the University of California, Los Angeles (1965) and the University of Helsinki (1971–1976).

Raimon Panikkar (1918–2010) specialized in religious studies, philosophy, and Indology. He studied at Barcelona, Bonn, Mysore, Banaras Hindu, Complutense (under Juan Zaragüeta), and Lateran universities, later teaching at Complutense, Harvard, and UC Santa Barbara (1971–1978; emeritus circa 1987–2010).

Raimond Gaita (born 1946) is a philosopher who studied at the University of Melbourne and the University of Leeds. He held professorships at King's College London (1977–2011) and Australian Catholic University (1993–2011), later becoming an Honorary Professorial Fellow at Melbourne (2019).

Raja Ram Shastri (1904–1991) worked in Indology. He served as a Member of the Lok Sabha from circa 1971 to 1977 and was attested as Chairman of the Managing Committee at Shri Lal Bahadur Shastri National Sanskrit University in 1976.

Rajan Gurukkal (born 1948) works in history, archaeology, and Indology. After studying at the University of Calicut and Jawaharlal Nehru University, he held posts at JNU, Mahatma Gandhi University (Director, 1988), and the Indian Institute of Science (2012–2016).

Rajan Khatiwoda (born 1984) works in Indology and history/archaeology. He served as a research assistant and cataloguer for the Nepalese-German Manuscript Cataloguing Project (circa 2007–2013) and was an editorial board member for the Documenta Nepalica Book Series (circa 2018).
Rajaram Hegde works in history, archaeology, and religious studies. As attested in 2010, he served as Director at Kuvempu University and as Director of the Centre for the Study of Local Cultures.
Rajat Verma works in computational fields and Indology. He has held positions at the Indian Institute of Technology Mandi and at BharatGen.

Rajeev Sangal works in computational linguistics and Indology. He studied at IIT Kanpur (1970–1975) and the University of Pennsylvania (1975–1980), and held posts at IIT Kanpur (1982–1998), IIIT Hyderabad (2002–2013, 2018–2022), and IIT (BHU) Varanasi (2013–2018).

Rajendra Chandra Hazra (1904–1982) was an Indology scholar who earned his BA at the University of Dhaka and completed doctoral studies under Sushil Kumar De. He lectured at Jagannath University and Dhaka, later serving at Sanskrit College and University (1951–1972).

Rajendralal Mitra (1824–1891) worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied at Medical College, Kolkata, and the University of Calcutta, and served as librarian-cum-assistant-secretary (1846–1856) and president (1885) of The Asiatic Society, and director of Wards' Institution (1856–1881).

Rajesh P. N. Rao (born 1970) works in computational fields and Indology. He studied at Angelo State University and the University of Rochester under Dana H. Ballard, and became a Professor of Computer Science at the University of Washington in 2000.

Rajkrishna Mukhopadhyay (1845–1886) was a scholar in history and archaeology. He studied at Krishnagar Government College and Presidency University (circa 1864–1866), and later held posts at Scottish Church College and Presidency University (circa 1878–1886).
Raju Rimal works in Indology, history, and archaeology. In 2018, he was attested at the National Archives of Nepal and served as an editorial board member for the Documenta Nepalica Book Series.

Rakhal Das Banerji (1885–1930) was an Indologist and historian who studied at Presidency University and the University of Calcutta. He worked for the Archaeological Survey of India (1911–1926) and held a professorship at Banaras Hindu University (1928–1930).
Rakra Tethong Rinpoche was a scholar who studied under Trijang Rinpoche and under Gendun Chopel from circa 1946 to 1951.

Ralf Kramer (born 1971) specializes in Tibetology. He studied at the University of London and the University of Hamburg under David P. Jackson, later working as Tibetan librarian at the Indian Institute, Oxford, and Aris Librarian at the Bodleian Library (circa 2006).

Ralph Abraham (1936–2024) studied at the University of Michigan and under Debabrata Sensharma. He held posts at UC Berkeley, Columbia, and Princeton, before serving as an associate professor (1968) and professor (1980) at the University of California, Santa Cruz.

Ralph Lerner (born 1928) is a philosopher who studied at the University of Chicago from circa 1944 to 1953, including under Leo Strauss. He subsequently held a post at the University of Chicago from circa 1953 to 2003.
